title: handoff-smoke-and-todo-joel
content:
Quick handoff / smoke notes from late-night run (me = Joel). Not a formal postmortem — raw notes for morning triage and things I need to finish.

SUMMARY:
- Night: intermittent p99 latency spikes on hosted-api route /v1/generate. Spikes correlated with ~300–600 concurrent sessions (burst from client X).
- Impact: transient tail latency (200–800ms extra) for ~12 min; no token loss or JSON corruption; clients retried and recovered.
- Temporary mitigation: added a per-route soft-concurrency cap and enabled CPU-side backpressure for that pool.

TIMELINE (local timestamps):
- 00:14 Observed first p99 bump in Alerts (latency -> ~1.2s).
- 00:16 Confirmed with trace samples: KV cache miss rate jumped from 3%->22% on pool A.
- 00:20 P95 stayed steady; p99 oscillating.
- 00:25 Applied quick policy: route X -> pool B (lower utilization), soft cap 150 concurrency.
- 00:27 p99 reduced toward baseline, KV miss back to ~5% by 00:34.
- 00:40 Elevated but within SLO after autoscale added one node.

WHAT I RAN / COMMANDS (copyable):
- watch -n 1 'curl -s http://metrics/internal?route=X | jq .latency.p99'  # quick monitor
- ./bin/collector tail --route X --last 15m --fields trace_id,kv.miss,slot_usage > /tmp/trace-x.log
- kubectl scale deployment pool-a --replicas=6 --namespace=dedicated
- rctl set-route-concurrency --route X --soft 150 --reason "night surge"

OBSERVATIONS / RAW SIGNALS:
- KV cache transiently filled with entries causing eviction storm; eviction_count spiked. Suspect pattern: many slightly different prompts (user metadata tokens) prevented prefix hits.
- Memory per-worker rose ~120MB during spikes (likely due to short-lived per-request buffers).
- CPU utilization ~60% steady; GPU utilization unchanged.
- GC/allocator logs show a burst of small allocations ~300k in 2m window.

HYPOTHESES (ranked):
1) Application-level request variety (user metadata injected into prompt) reduces prefix cache effectiveness -> higher KV miss -> more decode work -> tail latency. Evidence: trace samples show lower prefix hit ratio during event.
2) Worker-side allocation pattern triggers allocator slowpaths under certain concurrency combos (C++ arena churn). Evidence: allocator logs + memory bump.
3) Scheduling bump between pools A/B due to autoscaler mis-estimate. Less likely; autoscale looks normal.

IMMEDIATE TODOS (what I want to own in morning):
- TODO-1: Reproduce locally with loadgen script that simulates prompt variation. Add warm prefixes vs noisy prompts. Ticket: JIRA-INF-3421. (priority: high)
- TODO-2: Add a short-term prefix-normalizer middleware (strip non-essential session metadata) behind feature flag on experiment branch. (priority: med)
- TODO-3: Add metric: prefix_hit_rate by client_id and route; surface in console dashboards. (priority: high)
- TODO-4: Investigate allocator samples + heap profiles at spike time. Insert jemalloc stats around worker loops for next rollout. (priority: med)
- TODO-5: Draft a short runbook entry for routing quick-failover to pool B and when to scale. Put in repo under ops/runbooks/handoff.md. (priority: low)

FOLLOW-UPS FOR TEAM / PRS: 
- PR: runtime#1287 implements soft-route-concurrency API used tonight. Need code owner review (Mina).
- Perf task: engineering to evaluate prefix canonicalization in tokenizer step (can we normalize user metadata tokens?). Owner: Riley.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF:
- Was there any correlation with cache TTL changes? I didn't touch TTL last night but check infra-change log for 00:00–01:00.
- Need to validate whether prefix cache keys include client headers that we don't want — if yes, change key derivation.
- Consider making sample traces persist to S3 for 24h on p99 events to avoid stomping over logs.

SNAPSHOT METRICS (during spike window approx 00:14–00:26):
- p50 22ms, p95 48ms, p99 1.12s -> baseline p99 ~0.28s
- KV miss rate (route X) 3% -> 22% (peak)
- eviction_count pool A +420 in 10m
- worker memory delta +120MB

NOTES ON HYPERCARE / HANDOFF:
- Morning triage: please prioritize reproducer (TODO-1) before doing any kernel-level changes. If reproducer shows allocation pattern, we can proceed with jemalloc instrumentation.
- If similar spike recurs, escalate to SRE for temporary ingress throttling and consider enabling per-client rate-limits.

RANDOM SCRATCH/IDEAS (low effort experiments):
- Warm prefixes: maintain a tiny LRU of top-100 prefixes per-route on startup (fast-path).
- Small bloom filter pre-check for known-prefixes to clip expensive KV lookups.
- Add a quick metric: distinct_prompt_variants/min for route X.

PERSONAL REMINDERS:
- Ping Mina about runtime#1287 review first thing (tag her in PR).
- Schedule 30m pairing with Riley to sketch prefix-normalizer on Thu.
- Move reproducer branch into sandbox and attach to CI load test.

END — leaving monitoring watch on for another hour and will check slack.@channel if anything spikes.

Raw files I left: /tmp/trace-x.log, /tmp/alloc-snapshot-2026-03-12.txt
